metadata.note: Source: 05-commbank-agentic-ai-disputes.md (Sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 6.2). Central finding dramatized: two independently-confirmed CommBank AI systems — a thinly-sourced payment-disputes tool and a well-documented inbound voice bot tied to real July 2025 layoffs — have circulated in wider coverage as one autonomous 'Dispute Resolution Agent.' This reel corrects that CONFLATION; it does not claim anything new about CommBank's actual systems beyond what the case study already sources. B01, B02, B03, B04, B06 need new reel-scoped Remotion components (following the FluencySourceFlow / DtlChipGrid pattern of a fresh, props-driven component per reel, registered in Root.tsx) — none of these exist yet. B05, B07, B08, B09 reuse existing ready-made compositions (PredictCard, ClaudeVerdictArtifact, ClaudeComposerAsk, ClaudeTitleOutro) unchanged. GATE P has NOT been signed — see PEDAGOGY.md.

beats.narration_text: There's a bank at the center of a very clean story — an autonomous dispute agent that broke, and cost people their jobs. Habari — this is Liam, in for Bear. I checked whether the source for the AI and the source for the layoffs actually name the same tool. They don't.

props.command: There's a story going around about a bank whose autonomous dispute-handling agent went wrong and cost real people their jobs. Can you check whether the primary source for the AI system and the primary source for the layoffs actually name the same tool — and show me exactly where they agree and where they don't?
output: a disputes tool — real, thin, unnamed
a voice bot — real, and tied to real cuts
one narrative merges them. the sources don't.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Habari, Liam'; ask types itself
running indicator 'reading the primary sources…'
output lands: three teaser lines, the third one landing on the terracotta accent

beats.narration_text: Here's the version that goes viral: a bank drowning in fifteen thousand disputes a day builds one autonomous agent to handle them — and when it misfires, forty-five people lose their jobs. Two headlines, one tidy villain. Vendors even have a name ready for it: the Dispute Resolution Agent. CommBank has never used that name for anything.

show.event: sparkLine fades in over the cream stage
two labeled chips fly in from the record rack: the dispute volume, the headcount cut
both chips land inside one window titled the invented agent name
settle line lands in terracotta: 'lodges chargebacks. no human required.'

beats.narration_text: Pull the same two threads apart and the record splits clean. One thread: a narrow disputes tool, described once, by one executive, to one trade outlet. A completely different thread: an inbound-call voice bot, launched the same year, in a different part of the bank, with its own paper trail.

tracks.outcome: no headcount link — one interview, three functions

endpoint badges land, naming each track's real outcome

beats.narration_text: The disputes tool, graded on what's actually confirmed: it reads intent, checks the transaction against CommBank's own record, and lodges automatically once criteria are met — Chief Decision Scientist Dan Jermyn's own words, one interview, February 2025. No product name. No published architecture. CommBank's own December AI report doesn't mention it at all.

props.caption: Source: Dan Jermyn via Evident Insights, 20 Feb 2025

show.event: sparkLine fades in
three confirmed chips snap into place in order, dot lighting terracotta as each lands
fourth chip 'MISSING' snaps in muted, no dot
caption line names the single source

beats.narration_text: The voice bot, same treatment: launched June 2025, tied to forty-five real redundancies the union took to the Fair Work Commission, reversed within a month. At October's AGM, CommBank's own chair admitted it on the record — 'we made a mistake.' Real headcount, real reversal, real admission, and zero mention of disputes anywhere in it.

props.sparkLine: A real headcount, a real admission.

beats.narration_text: So which system actually caused the layoffs — the disputes tool, or something else entirely? Commit to an answer.

beats.narration_text: Neither card connects to the other. The disputes tool has no documented link to any job loss. The voice bot has no documented link to disputes processing. The 'autonomous agent that caused layoffs' isn't a cover-up — it's two true stories, read as one, because that's the better headline.

props.breakLabel: no reconnection anywhere in the public record

show.event: sparkLine fades in

breakLabel lands beneath the X in terracotta

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Two real systems: a thin, unnamed disputes tool — three functions, one source — and a voice bot with a real headcount, a real reversal, and an on-record admission. Neither one is the other. Five entries in, this series keeps finding the same reporting failure: real systems, real events — merged by outside coverage into one cleaner story. The rule that survives this: when an AI story and a layoff story get told together, check whether the primary sources actually name the same tool.

artifactLines: Disputes tool: real, 3 confirmed functions (intent · verify · auto-lodge) — one interview, no name, no architecture.
Voice bot: real, launched Jun 2025 — 45 of 90 roles cut, FSU → Fair Work Commission, reversed Aug 2025.
Neither system has a documented link to the other's outcome.
Five entries in: real systems, real events — merged by outside coverage into one cleaner story, every time.
The rule: no shared primary source, no shared story.

four verdict lines stagger in top to bottom
